subtitle: Shackleton Polar Regolith & PSR Water-Ice Explorer
brief_overview: Execute Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI), enter lunar polar orbit, and complete an autonomous soft landing on the illuminated rim of Shackleton Crater (89.9°S). Deploy coring drills and an autonomous micro-rover into Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) to prospect for cryo-trapped water ice volatiles.

nasa_flight_parameters.orbital_altitude_ratio: 100 km / 1,737.4 km radius (5.76% Moon radius altitude)
nasa_flight_parameters.spacecraft_scale_nasa: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO): 2.7m × 2.6m bus, 4.3m solar array span
nasa_flight_parameters.sensor_alignment: Nadir-pointing laser altimeter (LOLA) and Diviner radiometer facing lunar surface
nasa_flight_parameters.nasa_heritage_reference: NASA GSFC LRO Flight Dynamics & LOLA Science Investigation

nasa_landing_sites.name: Site Alpha: Connecting Ridge (Peak of Eternal Light)
nasa_landing_sites.description: High ridge connecting Shackleton to de Gerlache crater. Exceptional solar illumination and direct Earth telecom link; requires deployable micro-rover to traverse into dark crater floor.

nasa_landing_sites.name: Site Beta: Shackleton Crater Rim Saddle
nasa_landing_sites.description: Lower rim elevation with periodic shadow cycles. Good compromise between landing safety and proximity to volatile-rich cold traps.

nasa_landing_sites.name: Site Gamma: Permanently Shadowed Crater Interior (PSR Floor)
nasa_landing_sites.description: Cryogenic floor at 40 Kelvin (-233°C). Highest concentration of surface water ice detected by LRO LOLA/Diviner; requires nuclear RTG or massive battery storage and communications relay.

objectives: Perform precision Trans-Lunar Injection and 1.8 km/s Lunar Orbit Insertion & landing burn.
Execute powered terminal descent to soft landing at Shackleton Crater rim within 100m CEP.
Deploy 1-meter coring drill and autonomous micro-rover into permanently shadowed regions.
Survive lunar polar low-sun elevation thermal conditions and maintain communication line-of-sight to Earth.
Quantify sub-surface hydrogen and volatile abundance for Artemis In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).
engineering_constraints: Landing Delta-V: Braking from 1.7 km/s orbital speed to zero touchdown velocity requires high-thrust bipropellant propulsion and dedicated landing legs.
Extreme Cryogenic Thermal Environment: Temperatures swing from +120°C in sunlight to 40 Kelvin (-233°C) inside Shackleton Crater PSRs.
Communications Line-of-Sight: Lunar south pole topography can obscure direct line-of-sight with Earth ground stations; medium-gain horn or relay required.
Surface Mobility Requirement: A stationary lander on the rim cannot traverse the steep 30° crater wall without a dedicated micro-rover platform.
educational_context: Data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA altimeter, Diviner thermal radiometer, and KPLO ShadowCam revealed that the interior of Shackleton Crater is one of the coldest places in the solar system (40 Kelvin), allowing water ice to remain stable for billions of years. Water ice at the lunar poles can be split into hydrogen and oxygen rocket propellant, enabling sustainable human exploration under the NASA Artemis campaign. According to NASA GSFC flight dynamics, LRO maintains a circular mapping orbit at 100 km altitude (5.76% of the Moon's 1,737.4 km radius), maintaining active nadir pointing so laser altimeters and radiometers continuously target the polar cold traps below.
